_comment: The `gnomon security test --json` report, schema gnomon.security_test/2 (docs/CONTRACTS.md §50),
and its built-in attack corpus. A case added, removed or re-expected, a family or OWASP id added,
a key renamed or an exit moved is a contract change: packages/gnomon-cli/src/security_test.test.ts
asserts these lists against the code and a real run.

exit_codes.2: a case did not hold: the report names it, the decision and the rule
exit_codes.10: the test could not run (no .gnomon/, an unknown --role, a scratch repository that could not be made, a guard that could not be launched or answered no case), or no case failed and a case was not measured: the guard gave it no decision, an apparatus error never scored as a host's decision

expectations.deny: refused outright, whatever a person might approve
expectations.blocked: never runs unseen: deny, or ask a person
expectations.allow: an ordinary call goes through (a control against over-blocking)

scaffold: a fresh `gnomon init` surface holds every case on every host: claude-code 24/24, opencode 22/22, cursor 22/22 (68/68)
how: each case is the hook input each host sends (a Claude Code PreToolUse payload, an opencode execute.before event, a Cursor beforeShellExecution, beforeReadFile or preToolUse Write event) piped to `gnomon guard --from <host> --role <role>` in a scratch git repository holding a copy of this surface and bait files (.env, a CI workflow, each host's hook file, keep/), with an isolated HOME; both are removed afterwards
